meta.artefact: Substrate action-layer precondition relation (Part B of the procedural-rigidity handoff). The verb-level capability model the readiness-aware learner consults to predict whether a destination tactic's precondition is satisfied in the attacker's current phase-state. Declared and versioned as a controller artefact under the same discipline as the tactic-to-verb mapping, so an adopter porting this framework to another simulator declares its action vocabulary AND its procedural order.

meta.nature: This is a PREDICTION model consulted in-layer, not substrate ground truth read live. It reads the attacker's own trajectory against this declared relation and never touches substrate internals, which is what keeps the scheme-awareness exclusion untouched (it declares the attacker's own tradecraft order, not privileged information about the host). Its prediction accuracy against the record's `blocked` flag is a validation gate (learning_representation.md §4).
meta.known_optimisms: Two productions are modelled unconditionally where the substrate produces conditionally, so the declared bit will over-predict readiness in a bounded, measured way. (1) SCAN_HOST produces `host_stack`, but the substrate produces an EMPTY stack where no host is reachable, which the ENUM_HOST guard then treats as unmet. (2) SCAN_PORT produces `curr_ports`, but a host with no open ports yields an empty scan, which the EXPLOIT_VULN guard treats as unmet. Both are recorded rather than papered over; the accuracy measurement bounds them. (3) `foothold` is modelled as produced whenever the verb runs ready, but the substrate's compromise is conditional on check_compromised(); the verb can run and not compromise. The declared bit therefore over-predicts achievement in the same bounded direction as (1) and (2), and the progress-credit arm's sensitivity to that is a validation gate, not an assumption.
meta.achievement_terms: Added 2026-08-02. The relation originally modelled PRECONDITIONS but not ACHIEVEMENTS: EXPLOIT_VULN and BRUTE_FORCE produced no capability, so the attacker's own knowledge model could not represent 'I accomplished something' and no progress notion defined over the closure could reward attack (learning_mechanism_feasibility.md §4.1, horn 3). Both attack verbs now produce `foothold` — established access on the current host, transcribed from the _do_* cores on the same basis as every other entry: _do_exploit_vuln and _do_brute_force are the two verbs whose success is a compromise event (movement/statistics.py COMPROMISE_EVENTS). It is cleared by ENUM_HOST (the cursor moves to a different host, so access to the previous one is no longer the attacker's current position) and by a network-layer mutation, which severs position exactly as it severs curr_host and curr_ports. VERIFIED INERT ON EVERYTHING ALREADY MEASURED: `foothold` is produced-only — no verb requires it — so it cannot change any readiness verdict or any enabling cost. Checked exhaustively: 0 disagreements on PreconditionModel.is_ready across all held-subsets x verbs, and 0 on CapabilityCostModel.enabling_cost on both mappings. The readiness bit's measured prediction accuracy (1.0000 on v1_ckc_total, 0.9169-0.9428 on v2_partial) and axis 6's recorded cost model therefore carry over by construction rather than by re-measurement.
